notes: Trusted upstream sources (draft §23). This file answers three questions and nothing else:
which host may be contacted, what artifact a (capability, version) maps to, and where the
expected digest is published.
It deliberately does NOT contain digests. A digest written next to a download and never
checked against anything is decoration; the only acceptable source of an expected digest is
a published checksum file, and that is what `checksum` points at (draft §23.3-1).
`provenance` and `integrity` are separate on purpose (§4.4:368). v1 does no signature
verification: `signature` stays null, and a digest is never described as a signature.
Growth path: only hosts and capabilities that were actually verified end up here. An entry
that has never been resolved successfully must not be added 'for completeness'. Each entry's
notes carry its own verification status, and a test requires that statement to be present.
Draft §72 measured the `archive` capability against the real upstream and removed its entry.
The artifact template was right (`7z<version_nodots>-extra.7z` exists: 7z2603-extra.7z), but
the upstream publishes no checksum *file* on an allowed host: `checksums.txt` and five other
plausible names return 404 for every tag probed, and a release carries no .txt asset at all.
The per-asset digests appear only in the release page UI, which `single`/`sha256sums` cannot
fetch and parse. A digest source that does not exist is worse than no entry at all: `archive`
is now a capability without a source, so `source resolve` answers NOT_FOUND(1) — 'a capability
without a source is a reference-only capability, not an installable one' — instead of surfacing
an HTTP 404 as PROVENANCE_FAILED(7).
src-2 (draft §151): `node` was added — the first **runtime** source, and the first whose
artifact is a runtime *tree* rather than a single file. Like every entry here it was
resolved for real before it was written: SHASUMS256.txt carries the GNU-style line for
node-v22.14.0-win-x64.zip, and the artifact answers with 34906389 bytes. The artifact is a
`.zip`, so `source resolve` picks `portable_archive` (§145), and a plan for `node` is
`kind=runtime` (§150) — which is what makes the installed object a runtime instance.

sources.notes: ADR-0001: acquired through AIROOT's own plan/approval/fetch/verify/digest path, no admin, --no-modify-path. Verified online in draft §59: resolution, a 12721664-byte download through https_artifact, and a SHA256 match against this entry's published checksum file. stage/commit were NOT exercised there; they were exercised for real in draft §117 (plan -> explicit local issuance (ADR-0046) -> install FINALIZED, the same 12721664 bytes, digest identical to this entry's checksum file), and the payload was then run in §118.

a portable archive with no installer script; the checksum file lists the archive by name. Verified online in draft §59: this is the `sha256sums` name-matching path, and it resolved a real digest for the real filename. The artifact itself was not downloaded.

Verified online in draft §151: the first **runtime** source, resolved for real before the entry existed, which is what the growth path above requires: SHASUMS256.txt carries the GNU-style line for node-v22.14.0-win-x64.zip, and the artifact HEAD answers 200 with 34906389 bytes. `node` is a frozen `kind=runtime` capability with a whitelist predicate, so `source resolve node --version 22.14.0` is the whole operator route to an owned runtime — no new verb and no new flag. The version is one this machine really has under nvm4w, which is the point: the ledger can now account for a runtime AIROOT installed rather than only for one it referenced.
